disagreements.question: Can punishment-based training be effective, and for whom?
areasOfAgreement: Pet-owner community survey (Hiby 2004) found punishment use associated with more reported problems and not with higher obedience ratings.
IMDT and ABTC professional standards for Good Dog alignment reject routine aversive training.
disagreements.disagreementSummary: Authors of Hiby et al. acknowledge historical effective use of punishment in some expert training contexts while recommending reward-based approaches for typical pet owners; IMDT ethics prohibit +/-P and +/-R as training tools for members regardless.
likelyCauses: Different populations (professional working dogs vs pet owners)
Definitions of punishment and training quality
disagreements.goodDogPosition: Recommend reward-based methods only; preserve scientific nuance in evidence layer, not in owner default protocols.
researchGaps: Modern RCTs and welfare measures for pet dogs under different training regimens

disagreements.question: Do owner-reported 'fewer behaviour problems' with reward training reflect improved welfare?
areasOfAgreement: Dogs Trust cites owner reports and welfare-oriented reasoning for reward training.
disagreements.disagreementSummary: Charity guidance links reward training to fewer reported problems; Hiby uses problem reports as possible welfare indicators but causality is unproven.
disagreements.goodDogPosition: Present charity guidance with evidence typing; do not overstate causal welfare claims from surveys alone.
researchGaps: Objective welfare measures paired with training method data
